body_json.answer:
**Assessment:** rejected.

The new post's claim that lethal police force against Black people can go unaccounted for closely parallels [T4-009282](#T4-009282), which asserts that a "Cop who killed unarmed black man still isn't punished," and [T4-003024](#T4-003024), which asks why police who shoot Black people are not treated as criminals. [T4-009367](#T4-009367) extends a similar accountability narrative, claiming officers commit crimes "Yet there's no justice," while [T4-002635](#T4-002635) frames repeated killings of Black people by police as a recurring pattern needing wider dissemination. The main difference is tone and specificity: the new post is a hedged, general statement ("sometimes"), whereas the retrieved posts are more emphatic, name individual cases or hashtags (#BlackLivesMatter, #ACAB, #BlackSkinIsNotACrime), and in one case [T4-009247](#T4-009247) shifts focus to fact-checking public claims about police brutality rather than asserting impunity directly.
